thesis: Snowflake reported fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter ended 31 Jul 2026) on 2 Sep 2026 and the stock rose about 16.6% on the print, which accounts for most of the 26.1% 60-day move. Both published profitability metrics point opposite ways and both are quoted here: on a GAAP basis Snowflake lost $191.7M, or $0.55 per share, while the non-GAAP EPS of $0.62 came in above the roughly $0.26 analysts expected. Revenue rose 35% year over year, net revenue retention was 126%, and management raised full-year product revenue guidance to $6.07B, citing its CoCo AI coding agent reaching 9,100 accounts, up more than 2,000 in the quarter. The strongest counter-case is that Snowflake is still unprofitable on a GAAP basis and the stock has already repriced for the good news: even with GAAP still in the red, the loss narrowed from $297.9M ($0.89/share) a year ago to $191.7M ($0.55/share) while the company simultaneously raised its full-year revenue commitment, so the direction of both the loss and the guidance moved the same way rather than offsetting. This suggests demand, not accounting mix, is driving the quarter.
invalidation: net revenue retention falls back below roughly 120%, or the $6.07B full-year product revenue guidance is walked back at the next quarterly report

thesis: Corcept's 19.7% 60-day gain traces to its second-quarter 2026 results, announced 29 July 2026, the day before the single largest up-move in the window. Revenue was $256.1M against $194.4M a year earlier, with diluted net income per share of $0.36 versus $0.29. The new driver is Lifyorli (relacorilant with nab-paclitaxel for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer), which contributed $47.6M in its first quarter of availability, with over 1,300 patients started on therapy; the legacy Korlym and authorized-generic business contributed $208.6M versus $194.4M. Sources I read disagree on the ovarian approval date (one gives a PDUFA of 11 July 2026, the company update refers to approval in March 2026), so the launch timing is not something I can state with confidence, but the $47.6M of booked launch revenue is company-disclosed. The strongest counter-case is regulatory: Corcept received a Complete Response Letter in December 2025 for relacorilant in hypertension secondary to hypercortisolism and resubmitted the NDA in June 2026 under a roughly six-month review, so a second rejection around December 2026 is live. Even if that resubmission fails, the $256.1M quarterly revenue base and Lifyorli's launch economics are already booked and sit outside that decision, so a negative outcome would remove upside rather than the current earnings power.
invalidation: Lifyorli quarterly product revenue fails to grow sequentially from $47.6M, or the Korlym/authorized-generic base begins to decline year over year

thesis: Held position. Dell reported fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter ended 31 July 2026) on 1 September 2026 with revenue of $46.97B, up 58% year over year against roughly $44.92B expected, and adjusted EPS of $7.04, up 203%, against roughly $4.91 expected. Infrastructure Solutions Group revenue rose 89% to $31.8B on record AI server orders of $60.9B, closing the quarter with a $95B backlog. Management raised full-year guidance to approximately $192B of revenue (up $25B from the prior outlook), including $74B of AI-optimised server sales, and non-GAAP EPS of $25.50. The figures I could source are non-GAAP; a GAAP EPS was not stated in the reports I read, so the profitability figures above should be read as adjusted. The strongest counter-case for Dell has been that AI servers are a low-margin, working-capital-hungry business that grows revenue without growing profit: this quarter argues directly against that, because adjusted EPS grew 203% while revenue grew 58%, i.e. earnings grew more than three times as fast as the top line, and management raised the EPS guide by more than the revenue guide in percentage terms (roughly 150% versus 70% growth). That is the opposite of margin-dilutive mix. The $95B backlog also pre-funds several quarters of the raised outlook rather than requiring new orders to hit it.
invalidation: AI server backlog stops growing quarter over quarter, or full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance of $25.50 is reduced at the next report
sources: Dell Investor Relations Q2 FY2027 earnings call: https://investors.delltechnologies.com/static-files/a24f97e4-63b2-460d-a4be-44738826e8ce

thesis: Held position. Microsoft's 30.0% 60-day move is dominated by a single session at the end of July 2026 when fiscal Q4 2026 results were released: revenue of $90.0B, up 18% year over year, operating income of $40.6B and net income of $35.8B, up 31%. Azure growth was reported strongly, but the sources I read gave conflicting figures for it (one stating 43% in the fourth quarter, another 40% in the third), and I could not reconcile which applies to which period, so the Azure growth rate should be treated as unconfirmed here rather than quoted as a fact. Against the result, Microsoft has disclosed Azure capacity constraints that may cap near-term growth, and faces multiple proposed securities class actions alleging materially false statements about Azure growth, AI capital intensity and Copilot adoption between May 2025 and January 2026, plus new antitrust suits concerning OpenAI and Microsoft 365 and copyright suits from the Seattle Times and Newsday over AI training data. None of these has a scheduled ruling, hearing or compliance deadline in the next roughly 90 days that I could identify, so no active_litigation flag is set, but the litigation load is material context. The capacity constraint is a supply ceiling on an accelerating base rather than evidence of demand weakness; the counter-case is engaged but the unverified Azure figure means it is not fully settled.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerates below roughly 30% year over year, or one of the securities class actions survives a motion to dismiss with a scheduled trial date

thesis: Held position, and the only name this run to trip two criteria: a 13.6% 60-day move and a close within 3.0% of its 52-week high. Nvidia reported fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter ended 26 July 2026) revenue of $96.2B, up 18% sequentially and 106% year over year. Since then it agreed to acquire the AI developer platform Hugging Face for $12.9B total consideration, and declared a $0.25 quarterly dividend payable 1 October 2026 to holders of record 10 September 2026. On litigation, In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation (originally filed December 2018) had class certification granted on 25 March 2026, with Nvidia petitioning the Ninth Circuit on 8 April 2026 for permission to appeal; I found no scheduled ruling, hearing or trial date within the next roughly 90 days, so no active_litigation flag is set. The revenue figure I could source is a company disclosure and is unambiguous, but I did not this run find sourced evidence bearing on the strongest counter-case — whether hyperscaler AI capital spending sustains at the level this growth rate implies — so that counter-case is left unengaged rather than dismissed, which is what holds this at medium. The next binary event is Q3 earnings, estimated for 20 November 2026.
invalidation: quarterly revenue growth decelerates sequentially, or a major hyperscaler publicly guides down AI infrastructure capital spending
sources: Yahoo Finance / Zacks company news 4 Sep 2026: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/company-news-sep-4-2026-091500709.html

thesis: Lumentum's 12.2% 60-day gain is concentrated in 12 August 2026, when the stock rose about 13.6% to close at $932.47 after fiscal Q4 2026 results and fiscal Q1 2027 guidance both came in above expectations. Adjusted EPS and revenue roughly doubled year over year, and the company guided fiscal Q1 2027 net revenue to $1.225B-$1.275B, above consensus, on AI data centre demand for its optical and laser products. Mizuho, JPMorgan, Raymond James, Citi and BNP Paribas raised price targets afterward. The figures available to me are adjusted; I did not find GAAP revenue or GAAP EPS in the sources I read, so the doubling above should be read as a non-GAAP comparison. The counter-case is that essentially all of this growth is levered to a single AI optical-interconnect capital cycle shared with Coherent and Applied Optoelectronics — the same names in this watchlist that fell 13-14% over the identical window — so Lumentum's guidance beat and their weakness cannot both be signal about end demand. I do not have evidence this run that resolves which reading is right, and the guidance raise is a forward commitment rather than a delivered result, which is why this sits at medium rather than higher.
invalidation: fiscal Q1 2027 revenue lands below the $1.225B low end of guidance, or the company signals AI datacom order softness on the next call

thesis: Cerebras is the only candidate this run flagged on volume rather than price: 9.87M shares against a 4.54M 30-bar average, 2.17x, on a session in which the stock rose 11.1%. Both of the company's headline metrics are reported here because they diverge sharply. On a GAAP basis, Q2 2026 revenue was $180.11M, up 74.3% from $103.32M, and the net loss widened to $450.53M, or $2.98 per share; on the company's preferred 'core revenue' basis, the figure was about $210M against roughly $190.6M expected, and management raised full-year core revenue guidance to $880M-$890M. Cloud and other services revenue on a GAAP basis was $126M, up 281%. Separately, at its Supernova event Cerebras announced the CS-4 system entering general availability in the September quarter, and disclosed a $25.4B backlog driven largely by an agreement with OpenAI. The strongest counter-case is the size of that GAAP loss against $180M of revenue: $386.6M of the $450.53M loss is stock compensation, which leaves roughly $64M of other loss and makes the headline number substantially a non-cash equity charge rather than operating cash burn. What I could not establish is attribution for the 11.1% move itself — reports pair the Supernova announcements with a Morgan Stanley price-target increase on the same days, and I cannot tell whether the disclosed product news or the analyst action drove the volume, which caps this at medium.
invalidation: the $25.4B backlog is revised down or shown to be concentrated in cancellable commitments, or full-year core revenue guidance of $880M-$890M is cut

thesis: Corning fell 19.8% over 60 days, and the disclosed facts do not explain the move, which is the reason this is rated low rather than as a dislocation to buy. Q2 2026 results, released 28 July 2026, beat on both lines: core sales rose 17% to $4.74B against roughly $4.63B expected, and core EPS rose 30% to $0.78 against roughly $0.76 expected. Optical Communications, the AI-linked segment, grew 32% to $2.07B with Enterprise Networks up 65%, and Solar grew 90%. Third-quarter guidance of core EPS $0.85-$0.89 against about $0.85 expected and core sales of $4.9B-$5.0B against about $4.99B expected is roughly in line, marginally light on sales. The stock nonetheless fell about 14% pre-market on the release. These are core (non-GAAP) figures; GAAP results were not in the sources I read. Contributing explanations I found — optical growth decelerating from 36% to 32%, Apple reportedly scrapping a planned all-glass anniversary iPhone, and broad AI-sector rotation — are directionally plausible but do not add up to a 14% single-day repricing against a two-line beat, and I searched a second time without reconciling them. Management reaffirmed the Springboard plan targeting a $20B annualised sales run rate by end-2026 and $40B by 2030. This is unresolved evidence: the tape is saying something the disclosures I can read do not.
invalidation: Optical Communications growth decelerates below roughly 20% year over year, or the Springboard $20B run-rate target is withdrawn

thesis: Coherent's 13.9% 60-day decline is largely mechanical rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration, which is what caps this at low. The bulk of it is a single session, 10 August 2026, when the stock fell 14.23% to $325.18 two days before earnings, immediately after a seven-day run that had added roughly 71% to its market value including a 13.4% single-day gain. Reports attribute that drop to unwinding of a crowded AI-optics trade and valuation, not to company news. The actual results, on 12 August 2026, were better than expected: fiscal Q4 2026 EPS of $1.74 against roughly $1.58 expected, and fiscal Q1 2027 guidance of $1.85-$2.05 against consensus near $1.77, i.e. guidance above the Street. These are the adjusted figures reported; I did not find GAAP EPS in the sources I read. The counter-case is that the entire AI-optics complex is repricing at once — Applied Optoelectronics fell a nearly identical 13.7% and Corning 19.8% over the same window, while Lumentum rose 12.2% — and I have no evidence this run distinguishing a durable derating from position-unwind noise, so the fundamental beat and the price action remain unreconciled.
invalidation: fiscal Q1 2027 EPS lands below the $1.85 low end of guidance, or AI datacom bookings are guided lower on the next call

thesis: Applied Optoelectronics fell 13.7% over 60 days despite a strong reported quarter, and the evidence is genuinely offsetting, which is why this is low. Q2 2026, reported 6 August 2026, was the fifth consecutive record quarter: revenue of $191.9M, up 86% year over year and 27% sequentially, against roughly $190M expected, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.06 against roughly $0.01 expected and non-GAAP net income of $5.5M. Growth was driven by 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, with 800G revenue more than doubling sequentially, plus record CATV revenue of $80.6M, up 43.8%. The offsetting half is the guide: Q3 2026 revenue of $255M-$290M brackets the roughly $278M consensus, but non-GAAP EPS guidance of $0.11-$0.26 sits entirely below the roughly $0.28 consensus, so the company is guiding to more revenue at worse-than-expected profitability while funding a capacity build to over 650,000 800G/1.6T units per month by end-2026 and over 930,000 by end-2027. All profitability figures here are non-GAAP; GAAP results were not in the sources I read. A revenue beat paired with an EPS guide-down below the entire consensus is mixed evidence I cannot net out, and the capacity spend is the mechanism by which it could stay mixed.
invalidation: Q3 2026 revenue lands below the $255M low end of guidance, or non-GAAP gross margin falls below the guided 29% floor
sources: Yahoo Finance Q2 2026 earnings call highlights: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/applied-optoelectronics-inc-aaoi-q2-050943160.html
Wall St Engine (Q2'26 highlights and Q3 guide): https://x.com/wallstengine/status/2085458813931679893

thesis: Held position with no Step 2 signal this run — the 60-day move is 6.4%, volume is 1.09x baseline, and the price sits 26.4% below the 52-week high — so this thesis exists because held positions always get one, not because anything tripped. What I could source is industry-level rather than company-specific: NAND and DRAM supply is described as tight beyond 2027 with storage prices climbing in the high teens year over year, and SanDisk is reported to have contracted at a floor of roughly $0.29 per gigabyte, broadly in line with its Q2 2026 average selling prices. The stock rose about 8% on 4 September 2026 alongside Micron, on continued NAND pricing-cycle enthusiasm, and the company has initiated a $14B buyback. At an investor day SanDisk laid out mid-to-high-teens annual revenue growth for 2028-2030; the same report attributes non-GAAP gross margins of about 80% to those targets, which is difficult to reconcile with a NAND business and which I could not corroborate against a company source, so I am not relying on it. The read is therefore that a commodity pricing cycle, not a company-specific disclosure, is carrying the position, and the one long-range company figure I found is one I cannot verify — that combination is why this is low and why the thesis still supports holding rather than adding.
invalidation: NAND contract pricing rolls over or the roughly $0.29/GB contract floor is renegotiated downward, or SanDisk guides gross margin below its Q2 2026 level

thesis: Astera Labs fell 25.6% over 60 days on 1.91x normal volume, and the driver I can source is a third-party opinion rather than a company disclosure: the stock dropped sharply in September after Morgan Stanley argued that the Intel-Nvidia agreement to co-develop PC and data centre chips would affect Astera's business, including a 5.44% decline on 2 September 2026. The company's own reported fundamentals point the other way — record first-quarter revenue of $308.4M, up 14% sequentially and 93% year over year — and on 4 September the stock rallied on speculation about S&P 500 index inclusion, which is a flow event rather than a fundamental one. So the move down is attributed to an analyst's read on a competitive threat and the move up to index speculation, with no company disclosure on either side. That is a sentiment-driven repricing around an unresolved competitive question: whether Nvidia designing x86 CPUs with Intel displaces Astera's connectivity content is exactly the thing I cannot settle from what I read, and it is the thing that determines whether the 39.2% drawdown from the 30 June high of $499.48 is an opportunity or the start of a rerating. Avoiding is the honest response to a large adverse move whose central question I cannot answer.
invalidation: Astera discloses design wins or guidance showing connectivity content per rack is unaffected by Nvidia-Intel custom silicon, which would make the September derating an overreaction

thesis: Rocket Lab fell 22.2% over 60 days and is down about 57% from its highs and roughly 58% for the year, but the explanations I can source are a mixture that does not resolve into a clear company-specific read. On the operational side the news is good: Rocket Lab signed the largest launch contract in its history and closed backlog at $2.36B, and is working to close its acquisition of Iridium Communications. On the negative side, the company spends far ahead of Neutron, the larger rocket intended to change its cash profile, and Neutron has not yet flown — an execution risk with no disclosed date I could confirm. Commentary I read attributes the deepest falls to interest rates rather than to anything about the rockets, which makes a material part of this move macro rather than company-specific. Separately, an Electron launch was delayed by high winds and insiders sold $2.8M of stock. A backlog-growing company whose share price is being set by the rate environment and an unflown vehicle is a genuinely unresolved case: the bullish and bearish facts are both real and neither dominates, and the macro component is not something a company disclosure will fix.
invalidation: Neutron completes a successful first flight, or Rocket Lab demonstrates positive free cash flow, either of which would move the read from rate-sensitivity back to execution

thesis: AST SpaceMobile fell 15.7% over 60 days, and the largest single move in that window is explicitly macro rather than company-specific: the stock fell 15.5% on 28 August 2026 after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signalled that inflation was the Fed's focus and raised the odds of a rate hike, on a day when the S&P 500 gained 1.1% and the Nasdaq 1.8%. The mechanism is straightforward and is the company's own structural exposure rather than sentiment: AST is building a satellite constellation largely on borrowed money, so higher rates raise its financing costs and change the arithmetic of the build. Its own Q2 2026 disclosure shows the scale of the funding requirement — revenue rose to $31.5M from $1.2M a year earlier, but the net loss widened to $230.9M. A company whose share price is set by the rate path and whose operating losses exceed its revenue by roughly seven times is a macro-driven position, not a company-catalyst one, and the criterion that flagged it here is a price move that a rate expectation caused. That is a sector- and macro-wide driver, so this does not warrant an entry regardless of how the constellation build progresses.
invalidation: AST secures long-dated financing that removes near-term rate sensitivity, or revenue scales toward covering operating cash burn, either of which would make the story company-specific again

thesis: Intel fell 14.9% over 60 days, and the company-specific event I can source in that window is dilutive: a roughly $20B equity raise priced at $95 per share. Banks I read called the raise a net positive for the balance sheet while Bank of America and UBS trimmed price targets and identified 4%-5% EPS dilution, so even the constructive reading concedes the earnings-per-share cost. Alongside it, Nvidia has taken a stake of roughly 4% in Intel through a $5B common stock private placement tied to co-development of custom data centre and PC products, including Nvidia-designed x86 CPUs and system-on-chips pairing Intel CPU cores with Nvidia RTX GPU chiplets, and SK Hynix is reported to be considering Intel Foundry for HBM4E base dies. I could not reconcile the reported terms of the Nvidia placement: one report describes 214.7M-217.4M shares at $23.28 each, a price inconsistent with Intel trading near $95.89 today, which suggests the $23.28 tranche belongs to an earlier transaction being re-reported around a later regulatory approval. With the one clearly-current company event being a large dilutive raise, and the headline partnership's terms unverifiable from what I read, this is mixed evidence pointing at a share count that is rising faster than the earnings story is confirmed.
invalidation: Intel discloses foundry revenue from an external customer such as SK Hynix at scale, or the Nvidia co-developed products reach announced design wins, either of which would offset the dilution with committed revenue

thesis: AMD fell 12.6% over 60 days, and everything I can source attributes the move to sector-wide and technical factors rather than to anything AMD disclosed. Shares fell more than 4% through the $500 level during a broad semiconductor selloff in which the PHLX Semiconductor Index posted its steepest three-day decline since March and Nvidia shed as much as $153B of market value in a single session. The proximate causes cited are rising yields and macroeconomic uncertainty acting on a stock that had gained 126% year to date through August, i.e. profit-taking on a crowded position. Commentary I read also leans on seasonality — AMD has fallen in eight of the past ten Septembers with a median decline of about 5% — which is a pattern, not a cause. No company-specific disclosure appears in any of it; the sources explicitly frame the weakness as industry-wide rather than AMD-specific. A move driven by rates, sector rotation and profit-taking gives no company-level edge to act on, and seasonality is not a thesis, so this is not an entry.
invalidation: AMD discloses AI accelerator revenue or guidance that reprices the stock on company news rather than sector flow, which would replace the macro explanation with a company-specific one
